articles.title: Jason Wilcox: ‘best eyes’ at Manchester United or promoted too far and too fast?
articles.summary: Director of football is tarnished by recruitment record and Amorim stint but has received glowing review from above. Lisandro Martínez is not naive. At 28, he has experienced plenty in football and knows the causes of success and failure.
body: Martínez was not solely speaking for himself when, after United’s defeat at Atlético Madrid, he strongly criticised Wilcox. His views are shared by others at United frustrated by the output from above and who “expect” more from a director of football. Wilcox knows he is under pressure because the inadequate results cannot all be pinned on Michael Carrick, who is working with a squad unable to cope with the rigours of challenging at the top of the Premier League and facing Europe’s elite.

Clubs live and die by their recruitment, and United sitting 13th in the Premier League after one win from six matches does not suggest the squad is in rude health. A sporting director, like a referee, goes unnoticed when performing well but it has reached the point at United where players can take no more.

articles.title: Wilcox the target again in another damaging Man Utd fallout
articles.summary: Lisandro Martinez's explosive comments after Manchester United's Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid turn the spotlight back on director of football Jason Wilcox.
body: It is almost 10 months since Jason Wilcox was in the line of fire when Ruben Amorim gave the explosive post-match news conference at Leeds that triggered his dismissal.
Amorim was furious Manchester United's director of football had subtly advised him to change tactics for the previous game against Wolves.
"I will do my job and every department, the scouting department, the sporting director, needs to do theirs," said Amorim.
Less than 24 hours after that chiding, Amorim was sacked, and the focus was on the part Wilcox played in that.

articles.title: Manchester United teammates widely share Martínez view that Wilcox is failing
articles.summary: Defender challenged, though, by at least one teammate. Martínez out of contract next summer and plans to leave. Lisandro Martínez’s view that Jason Wilcox is failing as Manchester United’s director of football reflects the dressing room’s widely felt frustration at recruitment and squad depth…
body: Martínez may face internal disciplinary action over extensive criticism of the hierarchy made in two broadcast interviews after Tuesday’s 2-0 Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid. The players had Wednesday off so any action would not be taken before their return to training on Thursday.

Martínez directed his anger at Wilcox and what he referred to as “the top” of the club, saying recruitment had been inadequate in terms of volume and the scale of investment and that “more ambition” was needed. He said: “We don’t have the best squad at the moment compared with other top teams.”

Martinez’s comments prompted a challenge from at least one United player before the flight back to Manchester and caused tension to be heightened. The Argentina international did not appear to explicitly call out his teammates, saying mildly that “as players we have to do more”, and claimed that last season the squad had “created the base to build an amazing team”.
Although the sway of dressing-room opinion is with Martínez, his remarks are also regarded there as the centre-back eyeing his future because he is out of contract next summer.

articles.title: Kevin Pietersen tells ECB he will not promote gambling site while on England duty
articles.summary: Specialist mentor signed lucrative deal with online firm. Board’s strict code prohibits betting across cricket. Kevin Pietersen has told the England and Wales Cricket Board he will not promote betting while on duty as England’s specialist mentor.
body: The former England batter is contracted to work with Brendon McCullum’s white-ball team for around 150 days over the next 13 months until the conclusion of the 50-over World Cup co-hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. Pietersen’s betting ­interests create a potential headache for his employers.

The ECB’s anti-corruption code bans participants from “directly or indirectly soliciting, inducing, enticing, instructing, persuading, encouraging, facilitating or authorising any other party to enter into a bet in relation to the result, progress, conduct or any other aspect of any match or competition.”

The ECB does not take advertising revenue from gambling companies, has banned Hundred franchises from sponsorship deals with betting firms from next year and its regulations state that any counties accepting commercial gambling income must demonstrate that the proceeds are reinvested into infrastructure projects or community programmes.

All participants in cricket are also prohibited from betting, a rule that led to the England fast bowler Brydon Carse being given a 16-month ban – 13 of which were suspended – two years ago for placing 303 bets between 2017 and 2019.

articles.title: Watkins replaces injured Smithies in England squad
articles.summary: Kallum Watkins is called up as a late replacement to England's Rugby League World Cup squad after Morgan Smithies is forced to withdraw through injury.
body: Kallum Watkins has been called up to England's Rugby League World Cup squad as a late replacement after Morgan Smithies was forced to withdraw through injury.
The 35-year-old Leeds Rhinos second-row forward is set to take part in his fourth World Cup having previously featured in 2013, 2017 and 2022.
The loss of lock and second-row forward Smithies, who is set to join Perth Bears for the 2027 NRL season, comes as a blow to England.
However, in Watkins, head coach Brian McDermott has found a replacement he knows well having previously coached him during a trophy-laden spell at Leeds.

articles.title: Big scorelines, one-sided games - are Women's World Cup play-offs working?
articles.summary: The ease in which England saw off Greece in round one of the Women's World Cup qualifying play-offs showed just how inefficient the structure currently is.
body: The two-time European champions were superior in every sense as they won 8-1 on aggregate against a Greece side ranked 55 places lower in the world.
Realistically, Greece stood little chance in a two-legged tie against Sarina Wiegman's side despite performing well in their home 3-1 defeat.
England's resounding victory was not a one-off as Europe's other top nations, who were forced to drop into the play-offs, also met lower-ranked opposition and won emphatically.
It was not an evening that truly reflects the growth of European women's football, which has become more competitive than ever in recent years.

articles.title: Cliftonville's League Cup win overturned by NIFL
articles.summary: Cliftonville's hopes of a domestic treble are over after they were stripped of their Women's League Cup title for fielding two ineligible players in the final.
body: Beaten finalists Glentoran lodged a complaint with the Northern Ireland Football League (NIFL) following their 4-0 defeat in the July showpiece at Seaview and have now been awarded a 3-0 victory.
"The NIFL competitions committee found that the two players had not been correctly registered in accordance with the competition regulations," said the NIFL.
"The competitions committee acknowledges and thanks Cliftonville Ladies for its openness, integrity and full co-operation throughout the investigation."

Reds striker Caitlin McGuinness scored twice in the final, with sister Kirsty and Danielle Maxwell also on the scoresheet to deliver what the side thought was their fourth successive title in the competition.

articles.title: Six Kings Slam tournament in Saudi Arabia postponed until December
articles.summary: Tennis' big-money Six Kings Slam tournament in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia has been postponed from October to December due to unrest in the Middle East.
body: The tournament, which is in its third edition and awards £1.2m per competing player and an extra £3.5m for the winner, was originally scheduled for October 21-24, but has now been moved to December 27-30.
The six players included for 2026 are Carlos Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic, Alexander Zverev, Taylor Fritz, Alex de Minaur and Learner Tien.
The decision to postpone follows continued unrest in the Middle East and the recent bombing of the international airport in Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh.

"The decision ⁠reflects Riyadh Season's commitment to ‌delivering sporting events to the highest ‌standards, following an assessment of the organisational and logistical challenges ⁠associated with hosting ​the tournament ​and their potential ​impact on the ⁠quality of the audience experience," ⁠organisers said in ​a statement.

articles.title: Eagles’ ugly start has NFL considering pulling primetime game
articles.summary: Things have not gone smoothly for the Philadelphia Eagles this season. A last-second loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London over the weekend has Nick Sirianni’s side below.500. Things aren’t much better when one uses the eye test as Jalen Hurts has failed to get much of an offense going.
body: Philadelphia must now go about the work of chasing the New York Giants, who are a surprise presence at the top of the NFC East. And it sounds like they may have to do some of that work on a less prominent stage.

The Eagles host the Carolina Panthers this coming Sunday afternoon. Then the Dallas Cowboys come in for a Monday Night Football matchup eight days later. Results of those two contests will go a long way in determining if Philadelphia remains in its Week 8 Sunday Night Football spot against the Washington Commanders.

Rob Tornoe of the Philadelphia Inquirer reports this morning that the NFL is considering flexing that contest out in favor of a more alluring matchup. This would be the earliest the league has chosen to switch up a primetime game since 2024 when the Eagles-Jaguars tilt was subbed out.

articles.title: England rocked by injury on eve of World Cup
articles.summary: England have been rocked by injury on the eve of the Rugby League World Cup with Perth Bears-bound Morgan Smithies ruled out of the tournament.
body: Leeds Rhinos' Kallum Watkins is set to depart for Australia to take the place of lock and second-row forward Smithies.
Watkins, who played in two of last year's three Ashes Tests against Australia, will arrive in Perth ahead of the weekend but is not set to feature in Saturday's opener against Tonga.
Head coach Brian McDermott said: "It's really unfortunate what has happened to Morgan with an injury picked up in training.
"Morgan has been great since we entered camp. He's a real team player and his work ethic and toughness are qualities that we will certainly miss.
